```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.path = "figures/", dpi = 150)
dir.create("figures", showWarnings = FALSE)
source("R/00_data.R")
source("R/01_fit_models.R")
source("R/03_gof_summary.R")
library(kableExtra)

# p-value formatting helpers: "<0.001" for tiny values, bold when significant at 0.05
fmt_p <- function(p, digits = 3)
  ifelse(p < 0.001, "<0.001", formatC(p, format = "f", digits = digits))
bold_sig <- function(p, txt) ifelse(p < 0.05, cell_spec(txt, "html", bold = TRUE), txt)
```

# Overview

This repository contains the R code for the Venice sea-level analysis in \textit{Goodness of Fit for the r-Largest Order Statistics Method in
Extreme Value Theory}. It fits the **r largest order statistics** model to annual Venice sea levels (`r N` years, `r min(years)`--`r max(years)`, 10 largest values per year), compares models with likelihood ratio tests, and applies a new **parametric-bootstrap goodness-of-fit routine**, `rlarg.test()`, to each order statistic.

# Repository structure

| File | Purpose |
|------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| `R/00_data.R` | Loads and prepares the Venice data |
| `R/01_fit_models.R` | Fits models 1--5, likelihood ratio tests, fitted curves |
| `R/rlarg_test.R` | The `rlarg.test()` goodness-of-fit function |
| `R/02_gof_bootstrap.R` | Runs the bootstrap GoF tests for one random seed (slow) |
| `R/03_gof_summary.R` | Averages the p-values over all saved runs |
| `results/` | Saved bootstrap output, one file per seed |
| `figures/` | Figures generated when knitting |

# Reproducing the results

Run everything from the repository root. Required packages: `ismev`, `dplyr` (plus `knitr`, `rmarkdown` and `kableExtra` to rebuild this file).

``` r
source("R/00_data.R")          # data
source("R/01_fit_models.R")    # model fits, LRTs, fitted curves (fast)
```

The bootstrap (5000 simulations per model) is slow. Because of ties in the data, results vary from run to run, so the paper averages **10 runs** with different seeds (123, 234, 501--508):

``` sh
Rscript R/02_gof_bootstrap.R 501    # writes results/Results501.txt; repeat for each seed
```

Then `source("R/03_gof_summary.R")` averages the files in `results/`. To rebuild this page: `rmarkdown::render("README.Rmd")`.

# Data

Annual Venice sea levels: the 10 largest values (cm) in each year. The bold line is the annual maximum (order statistic 1).

```{r data-plot, fig.width=7, fig.height=5}
matplot(years, as.matrix(V2), type = "l", lty = 1, col = grey.colors(10, end = 0.7),
        xlab = "Year", ylab = "Sea level (cm)")
lines(years, V2[, 1], lwd = 2)
legend("topleft", legend = c("Annual maximum", "Order statistics 2-10"),
       lwd = c(2, 1), col = c("black", "grey50"), bty = "n")
```

# Results

## Likelihood ratio tests

```{r lrt}
lrt <- tab_lrt
lrt$`p-value` <- ifelse(lrt$`p-value` < 0.05, paste0("**", fmt_p(lrt$`p-value`), "**"), fmt_p(lrt$`p-value`))
knitr::kable(lrt, align = c("l", "r", "c", "r"),
             caption = "Each row tests a larger model against its simpler counterpart. Bold: p < 0.05.")
```

## Parameter estimates (Model 2: linear trend)

```{r params}
pt <- data.frame(Parameter = c("μ, intercept (cm)", "μ, trend (cm/year)", "σ (cm)", "ξ"),
                 Estimate = formatC(tab_params[, 1], format = "f", digits = 3),
                 `Std. error` = formatC(tab_params[, 2], format = "f", digits = 3),
                 z = formatC(tab_params[, 3], format = "f", digits = 2),
                 `p-value` = fmt_p(tab_params[, 4]),
                 check.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(pt, align = c("l", "r", "r", "r", "r"))
```

## Fitted annual-maximum curves

```{r fitted, fig.width=7, fig.height=5}
par(mfrow = c(1, 1), cex = 1.3)
plot(years, V2[, 1], xlab = "Year", ylab = "Annual Max", pch = "*")
lines(years, pred2, lty = 1)
lines(years, pred3, lty = 3)
lines(years, pred5, lty = 2)
legend("topleft", legend = c("Model 2 (linear)", "Model 3 (quadratic)", "Model 5 (linear + 11-yr)"),
       lty = c(1, 3, 2), bty = "n", cex = 0.6)
```

## Goodness-of-fit p-values

Bootstrap p-values (averaged over runs) for the correlation (R), Kolmogorov--Smirnov (KS), Cramér--von Mises (CvM) and Anderson--Darling (AD) statistics, for each order statistic *k*. Models 7, 8 and 9 have constant, linear-trend, and linear-trend + 11-year-cycle location parameters.

```{r gof-table, eval=!is.null(gof_avg)}
cells <- do.call(cbind, lapply(gof_avg, function(m)
  matrix(bold_sig(m, formatC(m, format = "f", digits = 2)), nrow = 10)))
gt <- data.frame(k = 1:10, cells, check.names = FALSE)
kbl(gt, format = "html", escape = FALSE, align = "c",
    col.names = c("k", rep(c("R", "KS", "CvM", "AD"), 3)),
    caption = "Averaged bootstrap p-values. Bold: p < 0.05.") %>%
  add_header_above(c(" " = 1, "Model 7: constant" = 4,
                     "Model 8: linear trend" = 4, "Model 9: trend + 11-yr cycle" = 4))
```

```{r gof-plot, eval=!is.null(gof_avg), fig.width=9, fig.height=4}
par(mfrow = c(1, 3), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))
for (nmod in names(gof_avg)) {
  matplot(1:10, gof_avg[[nmod]], type = "b", pch = 1:4, lty = 1, col = 1:4,
          ylim = c(0, 1), xlab = "Order statistic k", ylab = "p-value", main = nmod)
  abline(h = 0.05, lty = 2)
}
legend("bottomright", legend = c("R", "KS", "CvM", "AD"), pch = 1:4, col = 1:4, lty = 1, bty = "n", cex = 0.8)
```
